links.comparator_used: Traditional human forward-backward translation with expert committee review (English to Danish) of the Abdominal Hernia-Q questionnaire
links.outcome: Participant Likert ratings (1-5) of readability, comprehension, appropriate language and overall opinion; preferred version; ability to guess which version was AI-translated
links.effect: Before face validation (n=20), human translation was rated higher on all four outcomes. Medians were ChatGPT-4 4 vs human 5; p=0.008 readability, 0.004 understandability, 0.001 appropriate language, 0.002 overall. 18/20 (90%) preferred the human version and 18/20 (90%) correctly guessed which was AI. After face validation (n=18), there were no significant differences. Readability median 5 vs 5, p=0.341; understandability 5 vs 5, p=0.082; appropriate language 5 vs 5, p=0.359; overall 4 vs 5, p=0.100. 9 (50%) preferred human, 2 (11%) ChatGPT-4, 7 (39%) had no preference. 12/18 (67%) still correctly guessed the AI version.
links.tradeoff: The ChatGPT-4 version needed human quality control (an expert corrected outdated terminology and grammar) and face validation to reach parity. Earlier prompt versions produced omissions, hallucinations and altered meanings. Participants noted improper abbreviations and slightly less detail. Authors say ChatGPT-4 saves time and cost, but this was not measured. Findings are from one language pair and a small sample.
links.quote: After face validation, there were no significant differences between the assessments of the two versions of the questionnaire, their guesses were less accurate, and no significant difference in their preference was observed.

design_hint: Human quality control and face validation of LLM translation
